reason: The abstract confirms novel compound heterozygous variants in FREM1 were identified and speculated to cause the neonatal progeria phenotype in this patient. The paper directly characterizes FREM1 variants, fully on-topic for the FREM1 gene entry.

Published in Experimental Eye Research, this review focuses on the redox chemistry of Cys-rich gamma-crystallins (which CRYGD and CRYGS are) in the context of lens transparency and cataract. Directly relevant to both genes.

Although primarily a proteomics methods paper, the application directly studies gammaS-crystallin (CRYGS) peptide deamidation across normal aging and cataractous human lenses. CRYGS protein is a primary subject of the study, making it on-topic for the CRYGS gene entry.

The abstract reveals this is a craniosynostosis study of 101 infants; FREM1 appears as an incidental finding in only 1 patient out of 101. The paper's focus is SMAD6, FGFR2, and TWIST1 in craniosynostosis; there is no discussion of eye anomalies or FREM1-related ophthalmic phenotypes. The connection to ophthalmogenetics is too marginal.

Published from the National Eye Institute, this structural study of gammaS-crystallin (CRYGS) domain-swapping and aggregation is explicitly tied to cataract pathogenesis. Directly on-topic for the CRYGS gene entry.

Classic paper characterizing genetic heterogeneity of Usher syndrome type I with 151 families. MYO7A mutations identified in 64 families; USH1D (CDH23) and additional chromosome 10 loci mapped. MeSH terms include Retinitis Pigmentosa. Directly relevant to MYO7A, CDH23, USH1C, and by extension to the broader Usher gene set (ADGRV1, CLRN1) in the library.

The paper studies photoreceptor disc morphogenesis via peripherin and its suppression of ciliary ectosome release. ROM1 (retinal outer segment membrane protein 1) is a direct peripherin-binding partner essential for disc formation and is in the gene list. The abstract is fully within the photoreceptor biology scope of CDHR1, RAB28, and ROM1.

PROM1 (CD133/prominin-1) is the primary subject of this review. PROM1 mutations cause Stargardt disease, macular dystrophy, and retinitis pigmentosa; the review explicitly covers PROM1's role in cilia and membrane protrusions relevant to photoreceptor biology. Directly on-topic for the PROM1 gene entry.

Published in an ENT journal but MeSH terms explicitly include Retinitis Pigmentosa, confirming the ophthalmic component is covered. ADGRV1 and CLRN1 are in the library for their USH3/USH2C retinal dystrophy roles; a paper describing genotype-phenotype correlations across the full Usher syndrome spectrum (hearing + retinal) is directly relevant for understanding these genes.

Review of canine models of inherited retinal degeneration for therapy testing, with particular emphasis on corrective gene therapy. RPE65 and RPGRIP1 canine models are cornerstones of LCA gene therapy development. Directly relevant to both genes.

The paper studies AAV-delivered anti-clarin-1 ribozyme effects in the mouse cochlea (outer and inner hair cells, stria vascularis). Despite CLRN1 being a USH3A gene with retinal involvement, this paper has no retinal component and the finding (ribozyme-induced cochlear apoptosis) is a negative result for therapy. Too cochlear-focused for an ophthalmogenetics library.

Published in Ophthalmology, this case report directly investigates retinal structure and treatment potential in a patient with RPGRIP1-LCA (LCA6), using OCT and psychophysics to map preserved photoreceptors. Central case report for RPGRIP1 gene therapy candidacy.

The abstract directly reports a novel homozygous RPGRIP1 frameshift mutation (c.2608_2609insA) causing LCA6 in a consanguineous Emirati family, confirmed by NGS and Sanger sequencing. Textbook example of on-topic content for the RPGRIP1 gene entry.

The abstract confirms a novel homozygous RPGRIP1 nonsense mutation (p.C765X) causing LCA6 in Japanese siblings, with 27-year follow-up. Directly on-topic for both RPGR and RPGRIP1 gene entries, with detailed clinical and genotypic data.

The abstract describes molecular diagnosis of 106 simplex RP cases using a targeted gene panel; USH2A, CERKL, and RP1 are among the causative genes identified. Directly relevant to the CERKL, RP1, USH2A gene entries, and also to the Genetic testing topic category.

The abstract is entirely about BCOR aberrations in extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma. The paper discusses BCOR as a tumor suppressor in lymphoma pathogenesis. No connection to ophthalmology, eye development, microphthalmia, or structural eye disease.

The abstract covers novel BCOR-MAML3 and ZC3H7B-BCOR gene fusions in small blue round cell sarcomas. Pure oncology paper; no connection to ophthalmogenetics, microphthalmia, or structural eye disease.
The abstract describes ZC3H7B-BCOR gene fusion in endometrial stromal sarcomas. Pure gynecological oncology paper; no connection to ophthalmogenetics, microphthalmia, or structural eye disease.

The abstract covers human genetics of Tetralogy of Fallot and double-outlet right ventricle (cardiac defects). BCOR is not mentioned in the abstract or MeSH terms; the paper focuses on NKX2-5, GATA4, TBX1/TBX5, and 22q11 deletion. No direct ophthalmogenetics connection.

The abstract describes the crystal structure of a BCOR corepressor peptide bound to the BCL6 BTB domain, with application to killing BCL6-positive lymphoma cells. Structural biology/lymphoma paper; does not address BCOR's role in eye development, microphthalmia, or structural eye disease.
